scope: Managed Debian Firefox native audio and explicit helper application icon
causes: Both host audio capabilities were disabled in Stable Debian.
No matching glibc ALSA PCM plugin or default PCM configuration was installed.
Debian Firefox tried PulseAudio with no libpulse present; an overridable ALSA distribution default is required.
The system D-Bus was present, but there was no desktop session bus.

repairs.guest_plugin: Built on Debian ARM64 against libasound2 1.2.14 and glibc 2.41; not the Alpine musl binary.
repairs.alsa_configuration: asound-system.conf excludes the distribution-default include to avoid /etc/asound.conf recursion.
repairs.firefox_default: /etc/firefox-esr/trames-audio.js selects alsa; existing user preferences and sandbox remain unchanged.
repairs.session_bus: Stable root systemd service uses existing /run/user/0/bus; no runtime-directory remount. Dev shell test uses the standard guest daemon.
repairs.icon: CLI-hosted Wayland windows set the same bundled application icon as Manager before Dock activation. Installer refreshes the installed LaunchServices path.

limitations: Virtual microphone currently supplies silence; physical microphone signal was not tested.

Existing unrelated running environments were not restarted.
validation_notes: Playback, capture, full duplex and real Firefox checks passed in both channels. Dev playback clock regression also passed.
Both Mac channel builds and strict code-signature checks passed; native-window regression passed all three cases.
Execution-boundary guard passed. Unchanged shared-kernel/CPU/GPU results were reused.
Dev shell boot has no persistent session bus service; the normal guest daemon was restarted after deployment. Use dbus-run-session for a browser after a shell-only environment restart.
Audio/backend changes are environment configuration and payload deployment, not changes to the shared native audio ABI.
